content: Discussion for #Project announcements > Lean (meta-) programming cookbook @ 💬
Could you clarify whether this cookbook was vibe-coded or written by humans?
@Patrick Massot Written by humans. Strictly speaking I have copilot running in the background and occasionally take its suggestions so a small AI component. But not vibe coded for sure.
Thanks! I’m sure this will be very useful to many people.
I hope so. I hope others contribute too (especially things I don't know).
Great! Please add an entry on https://leanprover-community.github.io/documentation.html
Made a PR: https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/pull/821
Thanks!

About this, specifically

we generally have to work with so called Monads. We will not attempt to explain these here

I think it is useful to think of monads as bookkeepers or accountants. They perform "transactions", but also make changes to ledger entries behind the scenes, and keep track of where the bank stands.
Queue somebody mentioning burritos now :-)
Seriously, I'm not sure how far these metaphors really go: https://kjaer.io/a-monad-is-not-a-burrito/
I think the bookkeeping analogy goes far for state, writer, and except monads

Basically a monad is keeping track of some ledger book and updating it when you perform transactions to get computations. For IO monads the analogy is less clear, because one can do all sorts of things in IO
In lean's metaprogramming this is essentially what the metaprogramming monads do. They keep track of metavariables, term elaboration state, proof state etc, and update them as tactics are evaluated.
Everyone has their favourite views of Monads (me too). The cookbook deliberately dodges this.

For a more practical addition to that page, would a PR adding some explanation of how to use the different elaboration monads together (e.g. using TacticM within TermElabM) be welcome? I think it is a bit non-obvious when you need to reach into the underlying monads.
@Chris Henson That would be very welcome. Exactly what we meant by recipes. Command.liftTermElabM etc too.
Perhaps something like https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/wiki/Monad-map, perhaps with a little more explanation/context, could be useful on this point
Thanks @Bhavik Mehta . We should add a link to that.
I think some small example programs in each monad could also be helpful.
Yes. For example in CoreM we can look up declarations. If you have specific recipe-like ideas please PR.
This looks awesome!
Will it be a good idea to have a channel for this, to discuss in depth about any recipes on zulip. There exists github Discussions too, but considering Lean folks exist on zulip more.

Thank you for this awesome resource!

I noticed that many of the expressions on the The Expr type page don't compile. For many of these, the fix is just adding a backtick to some constants or adding a universe level. But for some of them the expression is wrong enough to the point where fixing it probably requires reworking the page. For example, the one on lambda expressions uses free variables, which is not allowed. The solution is either to use .bvar or to use mkLambdaFVars, which requires explaining more concepts. Also, the distinction between single and double backticks is not explained.

I was thinking about rewriting parts of this page to fix issues and make it easier to use, but I'm worried about duplicating information from https://leanprover-community.github.io/lean4-metaprogramming-book/main/03_expressions.html. Maybe it would be helpful to have a table with the elaborated and expr forms and just link to the metaprogramming book instead of explaining every constructor?

Also, should quote4/Qq be mentioned on this page?
Thanks @Niels Voss I wrote that chapter in a hurry and at that time did not know how to make it checkable in Verso. Will clean up tomorrow ( it is late in India)
Ok thanks! I'm still considering creating a separate document with a bunch of example expressions. Is this something that would be useful?

Yes sure you can extend the current Expressions with what you like, pls do link to pre-existing resources if needed. Since this is a cookbook, each example is more of a "how to do X"(even very basics too), any extension on Working With Expressions would be appreciated
You can create a discussion thread on github(for now) to discuss more into the details if you want to.

Yes, certainly. Thinking of the lambda issue you pointed out, I realised that this is why one uses the monadic withLocalDecl etc. So the best thing in the cookbook may be removing the wrong one and pointing to that recipe plus elsewhere
I was thinking of a table where in the left column you have the elaborated expression and in the right column you have the idiomatic code that constructs that expression
Thanks. That would be welcome

@Niels Voss I have partially fixed the issues in that recipe modulo merging by @Anirudh Gupta. Thanks again for the alerts.

Now all the code is correct. However, I have simplified things a bit as universe levels confuse me. As mentioned above, in the case of lambda and forall expressions the recipe now mostly says that it is best to use the Monadic constructors.

However, it will be very useful to have a more complete explanation in the form of a table as you suggested. If you can PR that will be most welcome.
